newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open weaker on currency's decline.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open weaker on currency's decline.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened weaker in quiet trade on Friday as further weakness in the Canadian dollar and a negative outlook for the currency weighed on prices, analysts said.

"The dollar has weakened off further and I think there just seems to be a bit of a negative sentiment as far as the potential for the currency. I think that's being reflected in where the bills are trading this morning," said a T-bill trader with one bank-owned brokerage.
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill softened to yield 3.29 percent from 3.27 percent at Thursday's close.

The Canadian dollar continued to languish at lower levels on Friday as it met with further selling by U.S. accounts. The unit opened at C$1.4009 (US$0.7138) against a close of C$1.3998 (US$0.7144) and hit a low of C$1.4024 overnight.
The Canadian dollar has weakened to two-year lows in recent weeks amid concern that a near-term rise in U.S. interest rates would not be matched by the Bank of Canada, analysts said.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill softened to yield 3.63 percent from 3.62 percent on Thursday.
The one-year T-bill softened to yield 4.30 percent from 4.26 percent.
The call loan rate traded around 3.0 percent, in the center of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range.
